gates.gate: origin gate (x-opal-origin-verify header; the Origin header is not read)
gates.condition: Runs before any route, after the OPTIONS return (index.ts:187-189). Passes only when the request carries x-opal-origin-verify (or X-Opal-Origin-Verify) equal to the current or previous slot of Secrets Manager secret opal/auth/origin-verify (originVerify.ts:35, 128-141). The Origin request header is never read by this gate; Origin only shapes the CORS response (index.ts:37-58), and http://localhost:5174 is in ALLOWED_ORIGINS (index.ts:33). A request from localhost:5174 passes when it reaches the Lambda through the distribution, which injects the header on the APIGateway-portal origin. The dev build does reach /auth through the distribution: the vite proxy target is CloudFront (vite.config.ts:86-87), and vite.config.ts:183-187 records that a direct execute-api target was refused by this gate. A direct execute-api call without the header gets 403 (index.ts:220-222). The gate fails closed on a secret read error (index.ts:215-218).
A failed origin check returns HTTP 403 with the fixed body Forbidden, before body parsing and before any credential is looked at.

gates.condition: Runs before any lookup. The key is sha256 of the trimmed, lower-cased SUBMITTED email, so it is per account and not per IP (throttle.ts:86-93). Table opal-portal-auth-throttle (throttle.ts:20). Threshold 5 counted failures in a 900 s sliding window (throttle.ts:49-50); then a cooldown of 30 s doubling per extra failure, capped at 900 s (throttle.ts:51-53, 152); never a permanent lockout. Refused with 429 and Retry-After (index.ts:481-486). Fails open on a throttle-table error (throttle.ts:111-113). A correct password clears the counter (auth.ts:104). Only failed attempts count, so a driver that signs in with the right password is not throttled.

q3.hash_scheme: bcrypt through the bcryptjs library at cost (SALT_ROUNDS) 12. No pepper, no secret and no HMAC layer (password.ts reads none). Stored as passwordHash (db.ts:141). The walker's own writer is Python bcrypt at cost 12 (ui_walker_account.py:146).

It validates nothing; validatePassword is a separate export (password.ts:41). A Node script that imports this module is the tracked route. The Python walker has no reusable hash-only function: its hash is inline in arm(), which also writes the password to SSM (ui_walker_account.py:145-147).
q3.how: The minting process generates a random password in memory, hashes it at cost 12, and writes passwordHash plus status active to opal-users-v2 with a condition expression. It never writes SSM. The driver then POSTs /auth/login with the in-memory value. On disarm it replaces passwordHash with an unusable hash, as ui_walker_account.py:184-189 does. No auth-handler change is needed: login reads only passwordHash (auth.ts:96; db.ts:141), applies no pepper (password.ts), and runs no strength or breach check (password.ts:36-39). The write needs DynamoDB write rights on opal-users-v2, whose IAM was not read.
